messages:
kia: Heads up: customers reported opaque fncall failures. Console shows a burst of schema rejects but traces indicate validator_score dropped below threshold, not a deterministic parse error.

raj: Validator score? I thought we were binary (accept/reject). When did we add scoring?

ana: small experiment on canary: we augmented the validator to emit a confidence score (0-1) for ambiguous unions and enums so we can do soft-fallbacks. Rolled to 10% yesterday.

tim: That was the canary I deployed. The gate currently uses score < 0.5 -> hard reject. But router has soft_fallback policy for 0.5-0.7 and I think billing still treats hard reject same as success for accounting reasons.

kia: The customer impact: their app saw higher throttles because console shows rejects as coming from the strict route and quota depleted. They never hit degen but quota looked consumed.

raj: Wait, router did soft fallback for mid scores but billing attribution remained on origin route. So strict route charged even when we served degen?

sec-bot: security note: sampled rejected payloads must be redacted before leaving validator. Use redaction=v2 pipeline.

ana: We have three issues then: (1) validator->router contract ambiguous (score semantics), (2) quota attribution not aligned with effective route, (3) console lacks visibility for score distributions.

tim: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Lower hard_reject_threshold to 0.4 on canary (less aggressive)
- Emit new telemetry fields: validator_score, fallback_taken(bool), effective_route
- Add console heatmap for validator_score by route and a filter to surface requests scoring between 0.4-0.8

billing: For finance: we cannot change billing retroactively. Short-term we can add a metric "fallback_imputed_charge" that flags when effective_route != charged_route so finance can reconcile.

kia: I like the telemetry additions. We should also sample full traces for score<0.45 and score in [0.45,0.7) with different sampling rates (5% and 1%). Ensure PII redaction.

raj: Operationally: if we lower the threshold and that increases downstream degenerate runs, cost may spike. Need cost gate: if projected extra tokens > $X/hr abort. Also communicate with sales/customer success.

ana: We can estimate projected extra tokens from historical fallback rate * avg_tokens. I'll add a monitoring alert to abort threshold > $200/hr and mute canary.

deploy-bot: deploy plan update: patch validator config -> roll to 10% now, canary window 30m, auto-revert if fallback_imputed_charge_rate > 0.02 or 5xx spike.

sec-bot: quick security check passed for redaction=v2 on sample bucket (read-only to eng-platform + sec).

raj: Dashboard UX: console should show a compact timeline: strict_route rejects, fallback runs, charged_route burns, and a toggle to switch charge attribution view (origin|effective|dual). Also link to sampled traces.

kia: One more thing: streaming fncall partial outputs can reduce validator_score artificially. We should confirm parser patches didn't reduce score in edge of streaming truncation. Add a parser metric for truncated_frames causing score drop.

ana: Good call. Will add truncated_frames counter and emit sample ids where parser saw EOF mid-json.

tim: Action items:
- @ana push telemetry fields + sampling config (owner: ana)
- @tim lower threshold and watch canary (owner: tim)
- @raj make a console mock for score heatmap + charge attribution toggle (owner: raj)
- @billing create fallback_imputed_charge metric and finance sync (owner: billing)
- @kia notify CS and prepare customer-facing note if revert needed (owner: kia)

kia: I'll schedule a 30m follow-up in 45m to assess canary metrics. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
